result.title: HSPR: Recovering Software-Agent Benchmark Scores via Hierarchical Posterior Inference
result.summary: Evaluating software agents on a full benchmark is expensive. A small task subset can preserve agent rankings while yielding inaccurate scores. Historical responses provide useful structure, but tasks with identical source responses can have different outcomes for a new target agent. We introduce Hierarchical Score Posterior Recovery (HSPR), which combines source-fitted response factors with uncertain group success rates. Observed target outcomes update the posteriors over the target latent state and group rates; posterior-guided acquisition selects subsequent tasks. Its score-based criterion equals the expected one-step reduction in full-score posterior variance. Observed successes and posterior-predictive counts for unqueried tasks yield a full-score posterior. The final estimate uses its median with source-selected calibration. At a 10% task budget on four task banks from the SWE-bench family, HSPR achieves the lowest mean absolute error (MAE) on three banks and the lowest maximum absolute error (MaxErr) on all four among the methods compared. Removing group uncertainty or replacing adaptive queries increases macro MAE in the respective controls. Macro MAE decreases across 5-20% budgets.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 HSPR，用分层后验推断把源智能体的响应因子与不确定的组成功率结合，观测到的新智能体结果更新目标隐状态后验，并按「预期一步降低全量分数后验方差」的准则自适应选取任务子集，从而在少量任务预算下估计软件智能体在完整基准上的分数。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「信息价值/后验方差」驱动的证据采集与预算-精度关系，可能与 LVR 评估中的动态计算、何时停止或继续取证据的问题表述相通，可作核查线索；但对象是软件智能体的基准评分，与视觉/多模态推理状态无直接联系，迁移属推测。
